first_half#fh_2h_tie.rationale: Verified on the Kalshi API (event KXNCAAMB2H-26NOV08ARKUVA): outcomes are home, away and TIE; TIE rules read 'If neither team wins the 2nd half (including overtime)' and only 2H points including OT count. first_half#fh_halftime_infra.rationale: cbb.halftime_state_adjustment already names the 1H-residual carry-over; the open item is its coefficient size (a regression fit on historical half scores) plus live-feed latency, neither of which is missing catalog content.

futures_champion#fc_balance_hypothesis.rationale: cbb.two_way_balance_profile is already defined and attached; whether it adds information beyond rating is a likelihood-ratio/out-of-sample test on tournament game results, i.e. an effect-size question data settles.

futures_champion#fc_coshare_payout.rationale: Verified: the live Big Ten series KXNCAAMBBIGTENREG-27 rules pay 1/N to each declared co-champion; the Big Ten shares regular-season titles on tied records (e.g. Illinois/Wisconsin 2022). KXNCAAMBBIG10REG has no events or rules text, so only Kalshi can say whether it will list and on which template; inputs unchanged.

futures_champion#fc_drift_calibration.rationale: The Nov-to-Mar strength-drift input is defined (stratified by returning minutes); the 2-3 point sd is a constant to be estimated from historical rating snapshots, a calibration not missing catalog information.

futures_champion#fc_r76_format.rationale: Verified: the NCAA DI Board of Governors approved (7 May 2026) a 76-team men's field from 2027: 44 at-large bids, a 12-game Opening Round of the 12 lowest at-large and 12 lowest automatic qualifiers. cbb.tournament_field_format is already attached to futures_champion and holds these parameters; the remaining title-path effect is a bracket-sim computation.

futures_champion#fc_secondary_field_rule.rationale: Verified (NCAA, 1 Oct 2026): the 2027 NIT shrinks to 24 teams; exempt bids go one each to the highest-ranked eligible team of the top-10 KenPom conferences, auto bids to non-NCAA regular-season champions with average metric rank <=125. cbb.secondary_postseason_field_model defines eligibility from NET rank only, so its rule table and required rank inputs are now wrong; 2027 Crown allocation is still unresearched.
futures_champion#fc_secondary_field_rule.catalog_action: Rewrite cbb.secondary_postseason_field_model measurement with the 2027 NIT rules (24 teams, top-10 KenPom-conference exempt bids, champion auto bids at avg rank <=125), add conference KenPom ranking and multi-metric average rank as required raw inputs, and research/record the 2027 College Basketball Crown conference allocation for futures_champion.

futures_conference#fcf_duplicates.rationale: Checked on the Kalshi API: KXNCAAMBIGTEN holds only a 2025 event (stale) while KXNCAAMBBIG10 lists 2026 and 2027; KXNCAAMBBIG12 is current and IG12/IGEAST/BIGEAST/BIG10REG list nothing open; KXNCAAMBWAC holds only the 2026 event and the WAC is verified rebranded UAC for 2026-27 (UAC series has no events yet). Inputs are unchanged; whether future listings use identical terms is Kalshi's call.

futures_conference#fcf_policy_source.rationale: Per-conference co-champion and tiebreak policy is already the defined input the settlement reads; what is unverified is whether every league publishes current versioned manuals, a source-coverage limitation rather than a missing input.

futures_conference#fcf_strength_sd.rationale: The shared strength factor is defined in the catalog; its sd by games played and the resulting co-champion frequency are constants fitted on historical rating snapshots and checked against history.

futures_seed_other#so_field_size.rationale: Verified: 2027 field is 76 teams (44 at-large, 12 Opening Round games of the 12 lowest at-large and 12 lowest auto-bid teams, First Four name dropped). futures_seed_other prices at-large/bubble and round-qualification series (KXMARMADROUND 'Round of 76') but does not attach cbb.tournament_field_format, so its input list is missing the format definition.
futures_seed_other#so_field_size.catalog_action: Attach cbb.tournament_field_format to the futures_seed_other record, record the verified 76-team structure (44 at-large, 12 Opening Round games, round labels) in its measurement, and update cbb.auto_bid_structure/committee seed-model text that assumes 36 at-large and a 68-team First Four.

game_moneyline_spread#ml_luck_wiring.rationale: cbb.three_pt_luck exists in the catalog and the record names the double-count question; whether adding it to the ensemble improves held-out margin error is an out-of-sample comparison, an empirical question, not missing content.

game_total#tot_base_rates.rationale: OT frequency and points per OT period are already inputs (cbb.ot_model, cbb.ot_period_tie_chain); the quoted 5-6% and 10-12 vs 15-18 points are constants to replace with measured line-score values, a calibration settled by data.

player_props#pr_cold_start_calibration.rationale: Transfer translation inputs (conference-tier discount, vacated-minutes pass-through) are defined; their magnitudes are calibration constants to fit on 2021+ transfers, with portal-era sample size a feasibility issue.

player_props#pr_scorekeeper_effect.rationale: cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias is defined with a concrete home-minus-away measurement; whether its college magnitude is non-zero is a dispersion test on public box scores, an effect-size question.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_numeric_assum.rationale: The assists-makes correlation, rebound pool mean/sd and shock loadings are parameters of inputs the record already names (rebound_pool, assist_conversion_chain, shooting_shock_loadings); replacing assumed values with box-score estimates is calibration.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_scorer_discre.rationale: The catalog already defines cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias for assists/blocks/rebounds and wires it to player_props, but the player_rebounds_assists record, whose assist props it targets, does not attach it; the record itself says no attached input captures venue assist bias. That is a wiring defect; the magnitude is then empirical.
player_rebounds_assists#ra_scorer_discre.catalog_action: Attach cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias to the player_rebounds_assists record inputs (secondary role, assists/rebounds) and add the venue-bias interaction to its mechanism text; magnitude testing stays with pr_scorekeeper_effect.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_shock_loading.rationale: cbb.shooting_shock_loadings is an attached input; the +0.6/-0.5 guard loadings are parameters to estimate from game logs by role with sampling error, a calibration.

player_threes#th_persistence_claim.rationale: The matchup input and its weights are defined; whether 3PA allowed persists more than 3P% allowed and what weights follow are split-half correlations on college data, an empirical check.

player_threes#th_trailing_magnitude.rationale: The trailing-team attempt-lift mechanism is already in the record; its 15-30% size and role dependence are magnitudes estimable from play-by-play by score state.

team_total#tt_env_gap.rationale: cbb.venue and cbb.neutral_site are attached; the half-of-margin split of venue effect into own points and any team-specific deviation are effect sizes to estimate with shrinkage on historical games.

team_total#tt_joint_pricing.rationale: cbb.team_points_margin_coupling is attached and defines k by role and spread bucket; validating the bivariate home/away points structure across buckets is a fit on historical scores, not a missing definition.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.rationale: Competing simultaneous vacancies are a real mechanism stage (rival openings remove candidates); the record's own mechanism review says no input tracks the carousel, and none of the 16 attached inputs (search state, program resources, availability calendar) models rival openings.

unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_prior_sc.rationale: cbb.kenpom_prior_drift already models the prior phase-out; KenPom blog posts give only partial guidance (prior worth ~5 games early, ~2-3 games once all teams have played) and no current decay formula, so the schedule is a weight to fit from KenPom vs a results-only replica.

unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u2.rationale: Rest and event-type covariates on repeat-tie rates are a hierarchical-model question over pooled OT periods; the tie-chain input exists, and the open issue is effect size and sample feasibility.
